root_cause.text: The log roundoff value was unconditionally set to the hardcoded minimum of 512 bytes (BBSIZE) when the superblock's log stripe unit was zero or missing, without considering the actual log sector size, causing misalignment on disks with 4k physical sectors and resulting in CRC failures during log recovery.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a fallback condition `else if (mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize > 0)` to use the superblock's log sector size (4096 bytes in the failing case) before defaulting to BBSIZE (512 bytes). The CVE description shows that with `sunit=0` and `sectsz=4096`, the kernel was incorrectly using 512-byte roundoff instead of 4096-byte roundoff, leading to "Torn write (CRC failure)" errors. The fix ensures that when log stripe unit is unavailable, the kernel respects the actual sector size from the superblock rather than assuming a hardcoded 512-byte minimum.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add fallback to sb_logsectsize for l_iclog_roundoff initialization when logv2 is not available, preventing incorrect default BBSIZE usage in certain filesystem configurations.
intent_record.what: Added an else-if branch that sets log->l_iclog_roundoff to mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize when logv2 is not enabled but sb_logsectsize is positive, inserted before the existing else clause that defaults to BBSIZE.
intent_record.how: This change extends the conditional logic for initializing l_iclog_roundoff to handle an intermediate case. Previously, if logv2 was not enabled or sb_logsunit was not greater than 1, the code would always default to BBSIZE. Now it first checks if sb_logsectsize is positive and uses that value if true, only falling back to BBSIZE if both conditions fail. This provides a more granular initialization strategy based on filesystem configuration.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally sets l_iclog_roundoff to the hardcoded minimum of 512 bytes (BBSIZE) without considering the actual log sector size (sb_logsectsize). When the superblock's log stripe unit is zero or missing, this causes misalignment on disks with 4k physical sectors, leading to CRC failures during log recovery. The fix requires using sb_logsectsize as a fallback instead of the hardcoded BBSIZE value.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit a6a65fef5ef8d0a6a0ce514eb66b2f3dfa777b48
Author: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 18 08:21:48 2021 -0700

    xfs: log stripe roundoff is a property of the log
    
    We don't need to look at the xfs_mount and superblock every time we
    need to do an iclog roundoff calculation. The property is fixed for
    the life of the log, so store the roundoff in the log at mount time
    and use that everywhere.
    
    On a debug build:
    
    $ size fs/xfs/xfs_log.o.*
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit FIXES the vulnerability rather than introducing it. The root cause was that log roundoff was unconditionally set to BBSIZE (512 bytes) without considering actual log sector size. The fix stores the roundoff value in the log structure at mount time (lines 1404-1407: 'if (xfs_sb_version_haslogv2(&mp->m_sb) && mp->m_sb.sb_logsunit > 1) log->l_iclog_roundoff = mp->m_sb.sb_logsunit; else log->l_iclog_roundoff = BBSIZE;'). This ensures the correct roundoff value is calculated once during initialization and reused throughout the log's lifetime. The subsequent changes replace all hardcoded BBSIZE/sb_logsunit logic with references to the pre-calculated 'log->l_iclog_roundoff' value (e.g., line 1865: 'count = roundup(count_init, log->l_iclog_roundoff);' and line 3480: 'unit_bytes += 2 * log->l_iclog_roundoff;'). This is a refactoring that properly addresses the vulnerability by ensuring the log sector size is correctly considered at mount time rather than being hardcoded.
